fit: two randomized active doses in an open-label Parkinson dementia or Lewy body dementia trial
assessment: One and two hallucination adverse events were reported in the respective active arms. Other Parkinson drugs changed. The trial gives neither a visual episode rate nor a dried fig comparison.

The 75-person trial reported a nonserious hallucination in placebo and a serious hallucination in the higher nilotinib arm. Adverse-event categories do not provide a dedicated visual episode rate or food comparison.

fit: multicenter randomized NILO-PD trial with placebo and active groups
assessment: The 76-person trial measured tolerability, central exposure and motor scales. It found little CSF exposure and no treatment-related dopamine metabolite difference. No ingredient comparison or prespecified visual episode rate applies.

fit: open-label extension of the 75-person Georgetown parent trial
assessment: Sixty-three parent-study completers were rerandomized to active dose groups. Hallucinations appear in event records. The extension is not an independent cohort and did not count food-timed visual episodes.

fit: Parkinson formed visual hallucination groups, NPI and receptor PET
assessment: Seven Parkinson patients with formed visual hallucinations and seven without them differed in serotonin 2A PET binding. The groups also differed in motor severity and treatment duration. The study makes no dietary exposure comparison.

fit: scan-time symptoms and case histories in Parkinson dementia
assessment: Four of five PET and autopsy cases had the hallucination item at scan time. Several clinical timelines describe visual features alongside sleep symptoms. These observations do not measure dried fig intake.

fit: cognitive phenotypes and ordinal hallucination item in Parkinson
assessment: The imaging paper uses item 1.2 of the MDS-UPDRS for presence and severity. Much of the positive item represents illusions or formed experiences with retained insight. No count of visual episodes by food exposure is supplied.

fit: Korean Parkinson K-NMSS composite and stage differences
assessment: The 323-person Parkinson sample reports higher perception problems and hallucination domain scores in advanced disease. The composite cannot identify a separate visual episode rate and has no dried fig exposure.

fit: NPI hallucination scale in dementia imaging groups
assessment: The 21-person dementia with Lewy bodies group had greater NPI hallucination scores than the Alzheimer group. That comparison differs in outcome, population and exposure from the dried fig claim.
The clinical DLB paper adjusts the hippocampal volume survival comparison for hallucination frequency. The adjusted statistic concerns survival. It provides no food-associated visual event estimate.

fit: Parkinson genetic case with visual symptoms during long-term care
assessment: The case describes visual hallucinations and brief antipsychotic treatment among other clinical changes. It does not compare dried fig consumption or count episodes.

fit: Lewy body dementia viewpoint and published caregiver accounts
assessment: The authors cite literature and caregiver experiences. The excerpts describe general safety and psychosis during care, with unclear visual modality and no food exposure or independent efficacy comparison.

fit: concentrated grapefruit juice drug-exposure crossover in healthy adults
assessment: Compared with water, double-strength juice raised serum nilotinib peak by 60% and total exposure by 29%. This measures drug pharmacokinetics with a different preparation and population. It supplies no raw grapefruit or Parkinson rest-tremor effect.
